summary: RETEST of the single bug fix: public_user() now includes placement_quiz_result. Verified directly via curl for a fresh signup + POST /api/auth/placement-quiz/complete with {correct:4,total:7} and {correct:0,total:7} -- the RETURNED response.user object now correctly includes a non-null placement_quiz_result ({correct, total, granted_lesson_count, granted_level, completed_at}) in both cases, matching what is persisted in Mongo. This was the exact reported bug and it is now fixed. Ran the full existing pytest suite (test_iteration_37_placement_quiz.py, 10 tests): 10/10 passed after adjusting one assertion (see below) that was testing the explicitly-excluded 20-lesson-cap tradeoff, not a bug. All regression checks (GET placement-quiz en/de/es localization + tier<=2, zero-score grants zero, double-call idempotency, PATCH /auth/experience, demo@tradequest.app login, /api/practice, /auth/me) pass.
action_items: No action needed. The public_user() fix (adding placement_quiz_result to the return dict) is verified working correctly for zero, partial, and perfect score scenarios.

The 20-lesson hard safety cap / low early-lesson XP interaction (partial score capping at level 3 instead of reaching target level 6) is a known, explicitly-accepted business tradeoff per the problem statement -- NOT re-flagged as a bug, matches previous guidance to raise separately with product owner.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 355 now correctly includes "placement_quiz_result": u.get("placement_quiz_result") in public_user() -- confirmed via direct curl calls that the API response (not just DB state) now surfaces the field for both zero-score and partial-score completions.

Adjusted one pre-existing test assertion (TestPlacementQuizCompletePartialScore) that incorrectly asserted 'len(granted_lessons) < 20' -- in practice a 4/7 score hits the 20-lesson hard cap (granted_level=3) by design, per the agent_to_agent_context_note explicitly excluding this from re-flagging. Test now asserts the cap is never exceeded (<=20) instead of assuming it won't be hit.

The 20-lesson-cap vs XP-economy design tension (previously flagged) remains unchanged as expected -- it is a known accepted tradeoff, not a bug, and should not be re-flagged unless the product owner decides to revisit it.
